notes: Rhode Island uses one uniform rate schedule for all filing statuses; 2026 brackets, standard deductions and the $5,250 exemption are from Division of Taxation Advisory ADV 2025-22.

Standard deduction and personal exemptions phase out when modified federal AGI is between $261,000 and $290,800 for 2026 (in $7,450 steps) and are fully lost above $290,800. Modeled as a straight-line phase-out.
The new high-income surtax (1% on income over $1 million) starts in tax year 2027, not 2026; the new $330 refundable child tax credit also starts in 2027.
Rhode Island EITC, property tax relief credit, and modifications (e.g., Social Security, pension, 529) are not modeled.

seDeduction.note: Rhode Island starts from federal AGI, so the deductible half of SE tax carries through.

seHealthInsurance.note: The federal self-employed health insurance deduction is part of federal AGI and is not added back.

retirementContributions.note: SEP-IRA and solo 401(k) contributions deducted for federal AGI carry through to Rhode Island.

qbi.note: The QBI deduction is taken below federal AGI, so it does not reduce Rhode Island income.

localIncomeTax.note: Rhode Island cities and towns do not levy a local income tax.

estimatedTax.threshold: Required if you expect to owe more than $250 after withholding and credits.
estimatedTax.safeHarbor: No underestimating interest if withholding and timely estimates cover the smaller of 80% of the 2026 tax or 100% of the 2025 tax (Form RI-2210). Farmers/fishermen use 66.67%.

businessCosts.llcFormationFee: $150 Articles of Organization (Form 400, Rhode Island Department of State).
businessCosts.annualReportFee: $50 annual report (Form 632), filed every year between February 1 and May 1.
businessCosts.franchiseOrMinimumTax: $400 annual charge for every LLC, including single-member LLCs disregarded for federal tax (Form RI-1065), owed for any full or partial year of existence. Sole proprietors without an entity do not owe it.
